task.title: Modifying your configuration file after deployment
task.shortdesc: To update your on-premises Red Hat Quay configuration after deployment, you can edit the config.yaml file and restart the quay-registry container. You can retrieve the file from the container if you do not have direct access to it.

ul.li: You have deployed Red Hat Quay.

context.p: After deploying a Red Hat Quay registry with an initial config.yaml file, Red Hat Quay administrators can update the configuration file to enable or disable features as needed. This flexibility allows administrators to tailor the registry to fit their specific environment needs, or to meet certain security policies.

note.p: Because the config.yaml file is not dynamically reloaded, you must restart the Red Hat Quay container after making changes for them to take effect.

context.p: The following procedure shows you how to retrieve the config.yaml file from the quay-registry container, how to enable a new feature by adding that feature’s configuration field to the file, and how to restart the quay-registry container using Podman.
